title: condenser operation
description: Condenser — the SAME unit as `phaseChanger` under a name that says which direction it is used in; it reads the identical operation block. Phase changer: condenses or vaporises a stream at a declared pressure. The outlet is fixed by exactly ONE of Q, outletState, outletQuality, superheat, subcool or outletT — whichever you give, the others are RESULTS. Alternatively give a `coolant {}` or `boiling {}` block and let the duty EMERGE from the surface and the film coefficient, which is the rating route.

P.title: Outlet pressure
P.description: Pressure the phase change happens at; defaults to the feed pressure.

Q.title: Imposed duty
Q.description: Absolute thermal power. One of Q / outletState / outletQuality / superheat / subcool / outletT fixes the outlet — declaring more than one over-specifies it.

outletState.title: Named outlet state
outletState.description: Ask for a state by name and let the duty be the result — the usual way to say 'condense it to saturated liquid'.

outletQuality.title: Outlet vapour fraction
outletQuality.description: Partial condensation or vaporisation to a declared quality.

superheat.title: Superheat above saturation
superheat.description: Leave the outlet this far ABOVE its saturation temperature.

subcool.title: Subcooling below saturation
subcool.description: Leave the outlet this far BELOW its saturation temperature.

outletT.title: Outlet temperature
outletT.description: Fix the outlet temperature directly; the duty follows.

coolant.title: Coolant side (geometry mode)
coolant.description: Present = let the condensing duty EMERGE from the film coefficient and the surface, instead of being declared. The driving difference is dT_film = Tsat − T_wall — the surface SUB-cools the film.

boiling.title: Pool-boiling side (geometry mode)
boiling.description: Present = rate the boiling surface. The driving difference is dT_excess = T_surface − Tsat, which is NOT dT_film and the run never reuses that label. The Rohsenow nucleate flux scales as (dT_excess/C_sf) CUBED, so a modest C_sf error is amplified threefold and the flux is treated as INDICATIVE (a ±100 % band) — there is no default C_sf and `citation` is MANDATORY, since C_sf is surface-finish lab data, not a fluid property. The reliable number is the Zuber CHF ceiling (±15 %), printed first; a design above it is HARD-REFUSED as burnout.

Csf.title: Rohsenow surface-fluid constant C_sf
Csf.description: No default exists. Surface-finish data for THIS fluid on THIS material.

citation.title: Source of C_sf
citation.description: MANDATORY — omit it and the run REFUSES. A cubed constant with no provenance is not a result.

geometry.title: Tube-bundle geometry (rating mode)
geometry.description: Present = the duty EMERGES from the surface and the film coefficients instead of being declared. Give the wall conductivity either directly (`wallK`) or by naming a material (`wall`) resolved in the assets catalogue.

orientation.title: Bundle orientation
orientation.description: e.g. horizontalTube — it selects the film correlation, so it is physics, not bookkeeping.

wall.title: Wall material
wall.description: Resolved by name in the assets catalogue for its conductivity.

wallK.title: Wall conductivity
wallK.description: Given directly, instead of naming a material.

condensation.title: Condensation model
condensation.description: Which film correlation prices the condensing side, e.g. NusseltFilm (laminar film, Nusselt 1916).

heatingMedium.title: Heating-medium side
heatingMedium.description: The heating-medium stream's inlet temperature and film coefficient — the other half of the rating.
